messages:
Anya K.: Heads-up: after switching nova-lite to INT4 on the priming-heavy routes we see a reproducible ~5-7% drop in top-3 exact-match for multi-turn primed flows. Seen in eval harness + 2% sampled prod traffic.
Ben L.: ouch. any failing examples we can triage quickly?
Anya K.: yes. quick snapshot (priming_slice_v3):
```
INT8: top3=0.83, MRR=0.62
INT6: top3=0.81, MRR=0.60
INT4: top3=0.77, MRR=0.56
```
Drop concentrated on long primed contexts (context_tokens >= 1k).
Sara P.: could be tokenization mismatch or cumulative KV precision loss. Did preprocessing change?
Mike R.: my hypothesis is KV quantization error accumulating across layers/time steps. INT4 reduces mantissa info for keys/values.
Anya K.: I pulled two redacted transcripts that flipped: one omitted a grounded snippet, one hallucinated a short answer.
Ben L.: can we diff per-token logits around the anchor? small shifts often explain EM failures.
Anya K.: pasted a micro-diff: 
```
idx=44: INT8 p(target)=0.24 -> INT4 p=0.12
idx=45: INT8 p(alt)=0.11 -> INT4 p=0.18
```
Ben L.: supports probability shuffle. Action: 1) repro in clean container w/ deterministic RNG, 2) run INT4 with KV disabled to isolate KV.
Anya K.: starting deterministic repro now. kicking off INT4+no-kv and INT6 runs.
deploy-bot: canary deploy 2024-06-14T15:22:30Z - model=nova-lite-int4 - rollout=10%
Sara P.: also sanity-check tokenization: earlier we trimmed a stray unicode joiner in preprocessing that might subtly change positions.
Mike R.: if INT4+no-kv matches INT8 perf, we have root cause. short-term mitigation: route long-primed requests to INT6 or INT8; keep INT4 for short queries.
Ben L.: cost math we should include for GTN/product: INT4 ~0.18x cost of INT8, INT6 ~0.55x. naive estimate: route threshold 512 tokens -> ~22-25% cost saving vs all-INT8 for this workload. need precise numbers for the scorecard.
Anya K.: I'll assemble a micro-scorecard: per-slice accuracy deltas, per-token cost, tail latency, A/B play, and rollback plan. ETA EOD.
Sara P.: include a presence/priming-fidelity metric (does expected snippet appear in output) and a 1k-sample of multi-turn priming with `disable_kv=true` + INT4.
Mike R.: if we confirm KV compounding, I'll open a trace ticket to eng-runtime: request matmul/attention kernel traces for INT4 path, and check accumulation error across seq positions.
Ben L.: ops: pause further INT4 canaries until triage done. deploy-bot can throttle to 0 if needed.
Anya K.: quick update 18m later: INT4 + KV disabled recovers most of the loss. numbers: INT4+noKV top3=0.81, INT6=0.82, INT4 with KV=0.77. So KV precision is likely the main factor.
Ben L.: solid signal. next steps: finalize scorecard, implement routing flag by max_context_tokens, and prepare short product blurb on cost vs UX risk.
Anya K.: attaching detailed CSV and example transcripts in the scorecard doc (link to doc coming).
deploy-bot: canary throttle applied - model=nova-lite-int4 - rollout set to 0%
Mike R.: routing plan: request header contains estimated max_context_tokens -> route >=512 to INT6, else INT4. I'll sketch a PR once the scorecard has exact cutover numbers.
Sara P.: product/GTN: prepare an external note describing expected savings, fallback behavior, and customer-visible changes. Keep messaging minimal: "we're tuning quantized model routing to preserve quality for long contexts."
Ben L.: thanks. action list recap:
- Anya: deterministic repro + scorecard (EOD)
- Anya: INT4 w/ KV disabled run & INT6 baseline (done/in progress)
- Sara: tokenization sanity check (low effort)
- Mike: prepare runtime trace request if we need kernel-level debug
- Ops: hold INT4 rollouts until routing or fix in place

Anya K.: will follow up with the scorecard link and the sample failure set. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Ben L.: nice work everyone. if runtime patch is nontrivial, routing+fallback keeps cost wins and limits customer impact. :thumbsup:
Sara P.: let's sync tomorrow AM if any new regressions show up.
